title: Number Systems
description: Learn the different types of numbers, how they are classified, compared, and represented on the number line.

content.title: What Are Numbers?
content.content: Numbers are symbols used to represent quantities, values, measurements, and positions. In mathematics and algebra, numbers are used to describe quantities and perform mathematical operations.

content.title: Using Numbers
content.question: What number represents the quantity of 5 apples?
content.solution: The number 5 represents the quantity because there are five apples.

content.question: What is one common purpose of numbers?
content.explanation: Numbers are commonly used to represent quantities, values, measurements, positions, and many other mathematical ideas.

content.title: Natural Numbers
content.content: Natural numbers are commonly used for counting. In this course, natural numbers begin with 1 and continue without end: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and so on.

content.title: Identifying Natural Numbers
content.question: Which of the following numbers are natural numbers: 1, 4, 7, and 10?
content.solution: All four numbers are positive counting numbers and therefore belong to the natural numbers.

content.question: Which number is a natural number?
content.explanation: Under the definition used in this course, natural numbers begin with 1 and include positive counting numbers such as 6.

content.title: Whole Numbers
content.content: Whole numbers include all natural numbers together with zero. They are 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, and so on.

content.title: Natural vs Whole Numbers
content.question: Is 0 a natural number or a whole number?
content.solution: Under the definition used in this course, natural numbers begin with 1, while whole numbers include 0.

content.question: Which number is a whole number but not a natural number?
content.explanation: Whole numbers include 0, while natural numbers in this course begin with 1.

content.title: Integers
content.content: Integers include positive whole numbers, negative whole numbers, and zero. They are ..., -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3, ...

content.title: Identifying Integers
content.question: Which of the following are integers: -4, 2.5, 0, and 7?
content.solution: Integers do not contain fractional or decimal parts. Therefore, -4, 0, and 7 are integers, while 2.5 is not.

content.question: Which number is NOT an integer?
content.explanation: Integers are whole numbers that can be positive, negative, or zero. 2.5 has a decimal part, so it is not an integer.

content.title: Rational Numbers
content.content: A rational number is any number that can be written as a fraction a/b, where a and b are integers and b is not zero. Rational numbers include integers, fractions, terminating decimals, and repeating decimals.
content.formula: a/b, where a, b ∈ ℤ and b ≠ 0

content.title: Identifying Rational Numbers
content.question: Is 0.75 a rational number?
content.solution: Yes. 0.75 can be written as 75/100, which simplifies to 3/4. Since it can be written as a ratio of two integers, it is rational.

content.question: Which number is rational?
content.explanation: 3/5 is already written as a ratio of two integers, so it is a rational number.

content.title: Irrational Numbers
content.content: Irrational numbers are numbers that cannot be written as a ratio of two integers. Their decimal representations are non-terminating and non-repeating. Common examples include π, √2, and √3.

content.title: Rational or Irrational?
content.question: Is √2 rational or irrational?
content.solution: √2 cannot be expressed as a fraction of two integers. Its decimal representation continues without repeating a fixed pattern.

content.question: Which number is irrational?
content.explanation: √2 cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers, so it is irrational.

content.title: Real Numbers
content.content: Real numbers include all rational and irrational numbers. Every number that can be represented as a point on the real number line is a real number.

content.title: Identifying Real Numbers
content.question: Is √2 a real number?
content.solution: Yes. √2 is irrational, and all irrational numbers are real numbers.

content.question: Which number is NOT a real number?
content.explanation: √-1 is not a real number. It is associated with the imaginary unit i.

content.title: Classifying Numbers
content.content: A number can belong to more than one number set. For example, 5 is a natural number, whole number, integer, rational number, and real number. Classification means identifying all the number sets to which a number belongs.

content.title: Classifying 5
content.question: Which number sets contain 5?
content.solution: The number 5 is a natural number. Therefore, it is also a whole number, integer, rational number, and real number.

content.question: Which number belongs to the natural, whole, integer, rational, and real number sets?
content.explanation: 5 is a natural number, so it is also a whole number, integer, rational number, and real number.

content.title: Comparing and Ordering Real Numbers
content.content: Real numbers can be compared using greater than (>), less than (<), and equal to (=). A number farther to the right on the number line is greater than a number farther to the left.

content.title: Comparing Numbers
content.question: Which is greater: -2 or -5?
content.solution: On the number line, -2 is located to the right of -5. Therefore, -2 is greater.

content.question: Which statement is true?
content.explanation: -3 is farther to the right on the number line than -7, so -3 is greater than -7.

content.title: Absolute Value
content.content: The absolute value of a number represents its distance from zero on the number line. Since distance cannot be negative, absolute value is always non-negative.

content.title: Finding Absolute Value
content.question: Find the absolute value of -8.
content.solution: The number -8 is 8 units away from zero on the number line.

content.question: What is the value of |-12|?
content.explanation: Absolute value represents distance from zero. Since -12 is 12 units from zero, |-12| = 12.

content.title: Number Line
content.content: A number line represents numbers as points along a line. Numbers increase as you move to the right and decrease as you move to the left. Zero is located at the center between positive and negative numbers.

content.title: Using the Number Line
content.question: Which number is farther to the left on the number line: -4 or 2?
content.solution: -4 is to the left of 2 on the number line because -4 is less than 2.

content.question: Which number is located farthest to the right?
content.explanation: Numbers increase from left to right on the number line. Therefore, 4 is farthest to the right.

content.title: Number Sets and Relationships
content.content: Number sets are related through inclusion. Natural numbers are contained within the whole numbers, whole numbers are contained within the integers, and integers are contained within the rational numbers. Rational and irrational numbers together make up the real numbers.

content.title: Classifying a Number
content.question: Classify the number -3.
content.solution: -3 is an integer. Since every integer is also rational and every rational number is real, -3 belongs to the integer, rational, and real number sets.

content.question: Which statement about number sets is correct?

options.text: Every integer is a natural number.
Every whole number is an integer.
Every real number is an integer.

content.explanation: Whole numbers such as 0, 1, 2, and 3 are all integers. However, negative integers are not whole numbers.

content.title: Ordering Real Numbers
content.question: Order the numbers -3, 1, -1, and 4 from least to greatest.
content.solution: On the number line, numbers farther to the left are smaller. Therefore, the order is -3, -1, 1, 4.

content.question: Which list shows the numbers in order from least to greatest?
content.explanation: Numbers increase from left to right on the number line, so the correct order from least to greatest is -4, -1, 1, 3.
